bibliographic.title: SARA: Leveraging LLM Agents and Jurisprudential Ontologies for Automated Legal Reasoning
bibliographic.authors: Francisco C J Bonfim; Sara Pessoa Silva; Alicia S Neves; Henrique Santos; João A Monteiro Neto; Jorge L B Araujo; Rilder S Pires; Ricardo Alexandre Da Silva Costa; Vasco Furtado; Vladia Pinheiro
bibliographic.citation_apa: Bonfim, F. C. J., Silva, S. P., Neves, A. S., Santos, H., Neto, J. A. M., Araujo, J. L. B., Pires, R. S., Costa, R. A. D. S., Furtado, V., & Pinheiro, V. (2024). SARA: Leveraging LLM Agents and Jurisprudential Ontologies for Automated Legal Reasoning. unclear.

methodology.method_family: system development and deployment evaluation with knowledge graph integration
methodology.study_design: LLM-agent platform architecture with modular pipeline and real-world court deployment
methodology.sample_description: Court of Justice of Ceará (TJCE), Brazil; regional Brazilian court deployment
methodology.technology_context: LLM agents, Jurisprudential Knowledge Graph (Jur-KG), OCR, legal ontology (LegalRelation, LegalGrounds, LegalClaims), competence questions for output assessment

eligibility.decision_rationale: The provided text strongly supports inclusion on LLM deployment in a regulated judicial setting with explicit governance signals (traceable reasoning, explainability, compliance, bias and privacy concerns). However, no explicit conversational, chatbot, or dialogue governance mechanism is evidenced in the excerpts; the focus is automated legal reasoning and decision drafting via LLM agents rather than conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Conversational governance fit is weak in the supplied text; full text needed to verify whether SARA includes interactive/conversational interfaces, human oversight workflows, contestation, or operational monitoring beyond abstract claims.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based only on front matter and partial architecture description. Deployment metrics, evaluation protocol, and limitations are referenced but not detailed in the supplied excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: Findings appear internally coherent and relevant to LLM governance in regulated legal contexts, but methodological detail on sampling, measurement, and limitations is insufficient in the provided text to support high confidence.

coding.theme: LLM governance through ontology-grounded legal reasoning in judicial deployment
coding.subtheme: Traceability, explainability, and regulatory compliance in court AI systems

synthesis.main_claim: SARA is an LLM-powered legal reasoning platform deployed in a regional Brazilian court that integrates LLM agents with a jurisprudential knowledge graph to support traceable, explainable judicial decision drafting while reporting measurable efficiency and quality gains and compliance with CNJ ethical guidelines.
synthesis.contribution: Empirical deployment evidence combining LLM agents with domain-specific legal ontologies and knowledge graphs for grounded, assessable legal reasoning in a real court setting.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for governance mechanisms (traceability, explainability, compliance, bias/privacy risk framing) and regulated judicial deployment of LLM agents; not primary evidence for conversational governance unless full text confirms interactive dialogue controls.
